idiom_name: JSON.parse/stringify for the wire form plus a compiled JSON Schema validator (Ajv) for the published contract
implementation_notes: JSON is JavaScript's own literal syntax, so the binding layer disappears: the published language is a JSON Schema/OpenAPI document, payloads arrive through JSON.parse (and leave through JSON.stringify), and Ajv compiles the schema into a validate() function at the seam, supporting drafts 04 through 2020-12 so the same document validates browser and server payloads. A hand-written parser plus dispatch survives only where a legacy or binary format must be spoken. Ajv's compiled validator is the closest thing JavaScript has to a generated binding: keep it at one ingress and fail closed.
pitfalls: JSON.parse turns numbers beyond 2^53 into imprecise doubles: ids, timestamps and monetary minor units lose precision unless they travel as strings - the schema should say so explicitly.
Validation is opt-in at runtime: any code path that parses without the compiled validator accepts arbitrary shapes, so keep one ingress function and route rejects to an invalid-message path.
Ajv instances are stateful (validate.errors, coercion and defaults applied during validation), so a shared validator with coerceTypes can mutate the payload it is checking.
